Novel Grader

Paste a story, open one or more .epub, .pdf, .txt, or .html files (or a whole folder), or import from a link to a page or a folder. Grading runs on this computer.

Some sites don't let other sites download their pages, block the public relays, or only show a story to logged-in readers, so links can fail. These ways always work:

1. Copy story bookmark (easiest). Drag this button to your bookmarks bar: Copy story for Novel Grader. Then, on any story page, click the bookmark. It finds the story text and copies it without the site's menus, tags, or comments, and tells you how many words it copied. On sites that split a story into chapter pages, it offers to load the whole story when the site allows that. If it picks up the wrong part of the page, highlight the story text first and click the bookmark again; it copies just what you highlighted. Come back here and paste into the text box.

2. Select all and paste. Open the story in your browser (use the site's single-page or full-story view for multi-chapter stories), press Ctrl+A (⌘A on Mac), copy, and paste into the text box here. Short menu, tag, and note lines are left out of the grade automatically.

3. Save or download it. Use the site's Download or Export option if it has one, or save the page from your browser (File → Save Page As, or Print → Save as PDF), then use Open files here.

Choose Stylized voice or first person when the narrator tells the story in their own voice and bends the rules on purpose, such as a dialect narrator who writes "I seen him," a stream of consciousness without apostrophes, or long run-on sentences.
The narrator's grammar slips and dropped apostrophes ("me and him went," "dont," "everytime") count like mistakes in character speech, at a quarter of the usual penalty (or not at all if character speech is set to Don't count). Fragments, comma splices, long sentences, low reading level, "I saw / I felt" filter words, and the odd tense shift are given more room.
Misspellings ("recieve"), confused words (their/there), misused phrases, "a" vs "an," doubled words, spacing slips, and clichés and other style checks still count as usual.
Characters sometimes talk incorrectly on purpose. A character who says "could of" or "your welcome" may be written that way to show how they speak, so it isn't necessarily the author's mistake. This setting only affects common errors found inside quotation marks. Narration is always graded in full.
Count lightly gives each one a quarter of the usual penalty and marks it "in dialogue." Count fully treats it like any other error. Don't count leaves it out of the grade and the report.

Several files

Chapters are joined in file-name order and graded as one work, with a grade for each chapter. Separate novels are each graded on their own and compared side by side.
